dimensions.title: How the score is built
dimensions.lead: INFORM combines Hazard & Exposure, Vulnerability and Lack of Coping Capacity with a geometric mean. Each dimension is classed on its own thresholds, so compare classes — not raw numbers — across dimensions.

region.desc: From a regional survey: every council in the region carries the same value.

national.label: National
national.desc: A national or INFORM SADC baseline value applied to every unit.

overlay.label: Overlay
overlay.desc: A documented hazard overlay mapped from expert sources, rather than a measured statistic.

noData.body: “No data” means no value was reported. INFORM leaves it out of the category average — it is never treated as zero, and zero is a real, low score.
noData.tooltip: No value reported — left out of the average, not counted as zero.

eprp.name: Emergency preparedness and response plan
eprp.desc: An approved, costed plan for preparing for and responding to emergencies.

aa.name: Anticipatory action
aa.desc: Pre-agreed actions and financing, triggered by a forecast before a hazard strikes.

eocc.name: Emergency operations and communication centre
eocc.desc: A facility that coordinates the response and communication during emergencies.

services.drrSource: Source: PMO – Disaster Management Department and district disaster-management committee records.

steps.indicators: Each indicator is scored from 0 to 10, where higher always means more risk.
steps.categories: A category is the average of its indicators; indicators without data are skipped, never counted as zero.
steps.dimensions: A dimension combines its categories with INFORM’s scaled geometric mean, rounded to one decimal.
steps.risk: INFORM Risk is the cube root of Hazard & Exposure × Vulnerability × Lack of Coping Capacity.

level.council: Councils share their INFORM source unit’s vulnerability and coping data because household surveys have no council breakdown.
level.region: Regions are rebuilt from their councils’ indicator averages rather than by averaging council risk scores: the INFORM combination is not linear, so the two would give different results.
level.source: INFORM source units: the district-level backbone of the Tanzania INFORM workbook, used here as the reference level.
level.national: The national value ({{value}}) is used as published in the INFORM Tanzania workbook, so it can differ from any average of councils or regions.

method.officialNote: The national value shown for comparison ({{value}}) is the official INFORM Tanzania figure.
